investigations.name: adhesion-calibration
investigations.objective: Are the two substrates' mechanics defined and parameterized so that they are mechanically comparable -- per cell type and per type pair -- and which vertex parameters are fixed by the CPM, which must be calibrated, and which cannot be?
investigations.claim: RE-CALIBRATED 2026-11-05 for the in-sheet immune vertex substrate (immune cells are half-size polygons in the sheet; reconnect p_4 = 1, T1 at 0.2 x side). Tension scale 1.683 (area 22.97 vs CPM 22.98). Both motilities are fold-free CAPS: epithelium 26.6 (MSD 2.2 vs CPM 9.5 um^2; fit 81), in-sheet immune 56.1 (displacement 4.6 vs 9.4 um; fit 214). Tension noise 5 (area CV 0.038 vs 0.093; 10 and 20 fold). Chemotaxis unchanged (scale 3.54, saturation 105). At kappa = 8 the small sheet now collapses completely (area 0). Earlier calibration (2026-10-28, overlay immune layer):   REVISED per the 2026-10-28 vertex-mechanics review. Both substrates' mechanics are now DEFINED term by term (docs/mechanics.md). Every vertex parameter is either energy-matched to its CPM counterpart (area stiffness K = 2 lambda_volume, per cell type), lowered per type PAIR from the blueprint adhesion table (Lambda_ab = kappa * J_ab, ratios fixed by J), or CALIBRATED to measured CPM behaviour on the Sego initial state, under a hard mesh-validity constraint (no folded faces). With per-pair junction tension actually applied and auto_reconnect ON, the tension scale IS identifiable from mean cell area: kappa = 1.74 gives area 22.8 vs CPM 23.0. Immune random-walk displacement (9.4 vs 9.4 um) and the saturating chemotactic drift curve are matched. NOT matched: epithelial wandering. The CPM-matching motility folds the vertex mesh, so it is capped at the largest fold-free value and the vertex epithelium wanders about 5x less (MSD 2.0 vs 9.5 um^2), though it does exchange neighbours (T1s). Area dispersion is not matched either (CV 0.033 vs 0.093), and the kappa that fits the small isolated sheet differs (~4).

investigations.name: bp-01-blueprint-schema
investigations.title: BP-01 — the blueprint as a versioned, backend-neutral artifact
investigations.objective: Can the biological blueprint be specified as a versioned, backend-neutral, statically-validated artifact, independent of CPM/vertex implementations?
investigations.claim: Stage 1 / BP-01 of the review program. The canonical blueprint is now a VERSIONED, backend-neutral artifact with a checked contract and a static validator -- the first of the three claims (blueprint fidelity) made a first-class, tested object rather than an implicit input. Specifically: (a) a `blueprint_version` field + versioned JSON schema; (b) a canonical/backend split (CompileOptions) so backend/run parameters (tension_scale, rules_seed) are kept OUT of the canonical biological state and recorded separately; (c) a static validator (`validate_blueprint` + `multicell-blueprint validate`) that reports structured diagnostics (errors AND contract warnings), not a success badge; (d) three hand-authored worked examples that validate and compile identically to BOTH backends.

investigations.name: crossparadigm-equivalence
investigations.title: Backend equivalence (TOST)
investigations.objective: Are CPM and vertex EQUIVALENT (not merely "not-distinguishable") under replication -- and on which outcome: cell fate, exact spatial position, or both?
investigations.claim: RE-RUN 2026-11-05 on the in-sheet immune vertex substrate (immune cells are smaller polygons attached to the tissue margin; faster reconnect; re-calibrated motility). Verdicts unchanged: FATE equivalent (Delta -0.0014, cluster CI [-0.0034, +0.0008] inside +/-0.05); exact POSITION not equivalent (same 0.674, cross 0.547, Delta +0.126, cluster CI [+0.070, +0.181] vs +/-0.10). Diagnostic split: the gap is not only the immune margin attachment (t0 offset up to 5.6 um) -- the epithelium alone is also not equivalent (same 0.738, cross 0.622, Delta +0.116); immune-only Delta +0.156. Earlier reading (2026-10-28) kept for provenance: SCOPED to Claim 3 (scientific equivalence) -- NOT blueprint fidelity, NOT biological validity. RE-RUN 2026-10-28 on the revised vertex substrate (hexagonal sheet, immune overlay, auto_reconnect, per-pair tension, CPM-calibrated motility) with mechanics-stochastic replicates. On cell FATE the substrates remain equivalent under the dependence-aware run-cluster bootstrap: Delta(same-cross) -0.0014, 90% CI [-0.0034, +0.0008], inside +/-0.05 (margin not yet biologically justified). On exact POSITION they are still NOT equivalent, but the gap shrank about 7-fold: cross 0.472 vs same-backend 0.608 (Delta +0.135, cluster CI [+0.071, +0.210] vs margin +/-0.10). The previous spatial gap (cross 0.083 vs same 1.000) mostly reflected a degenerate null. Replicates differed only in rule draws, so same-backend positions were identical by construction, and the vertex cells barely moved.

investigations.name: dose-response-crossparadigm
investigations.objective: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?
investigations.claim: RE-RUN 2026-11-05 on the in-sheet immune vertex substrate (re-calibrated motility): figure regenerated; the STRICT-DIRECTION behavior test (highest dose ends with more infection than the lowest, on both backends) still passes. Earlier reading:   Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

investigations.name: flu-lung-crossparadigm
investigations.objective: Does one backend-neutral blueprint reproduce the Sego 2022 influenza model on two different mechanical substrates, and -- judged against same-backend seed noise -- do the substrates diverge?
investigations.claim: REVISED 2026-11-05 (reviewer feedback: vertex CD8/NK floated free of the tissue): vertex immune cells are now SMALLER POLYGONS IN THE EPITHELIAL SHEET, attached at the tissue margin and moving along it by neighbour exchange, as the CPM immune pool wets the epithelial edge; reconnect resolves merged rosettes faster (p_4 = 1, T1 at 0.2 x side); motilities re-calibrated under the no-fold cap. On this substrate FATE still falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross 0.948 vs 0.926-0.960), but infected-patch OCCUPANCY (IoU 0.053, below both baselines 0.100 / 0.299) and LOCATION (centroid distance 5.7 vs 3.3 um) now separate the backends -- a candidate substrate signal, not yet causally attributed. Earlier reading (2026-10-28, overlay immune layer) kept for provenance: The ONE backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint compiles to BOTH the CPM (viva-cpm) and vertex (vivarium-tyssue) substrates and runs the Sego model WITH NAMED DEVIATIONS (V/L/C/F producers absent, latent-pool recruitment approximation) end-to-end on each. RE-RUN 2026-10-28 on the REVISED vertex substrate: a hexagonal one-polygon-per-cell sheet, immune overlay, auto_reconnect, per-pair tension, domain walls, and CPM-calibrated motility under a no-fold constraint. Vertex cells now move within the tissue and exchange neighbours, though the epithelium wanders ~5x less than on the CPM. Replicate runs are now also stochastic in their MECHANICS, so the same-backend null control includes mechanical noise. Against that null, cell FATE, infected-patch OCCUPANCY and patch LOCATION all fall inside the same-backend seed spread (fail to reject). The one candidate substrate signal left: the vertex I-count leaves the narrow CPM 3-seed envelope for ~45% of steps by N=400.

investigations.name: initial-state-fidelity
investigations.objective: Do both substrates faithfully reproduce the blueprint's initial centroids, sizes and types, with one vertex polygon per blueprint cell?
investigations.claim: REVISED 2026-11-05: the vertex t0 is now ONE sheet of 48 hexagons (36 epithelial + 12 latent immune), the immune cells attached at the tissue margin site nearest their centroid instead of sitting as overlay islands on it. Epithelial centroid residual unchanged (rms 1.60, max 2.44 um); the immune cells move up to one cell diameter onto the margin (rms 4.11, max 5.60 um), closing the CPM's medium gap. All 48 cells present, types exact. Earlier reading (2026-10-28):   REVISED per the 2026-10-28 vertex-mechanics review. Both backends reproduce the blueprint's t=0 state (every cell's centroid, size and type), with every vertex polygon corresponding to exactly ONE Sego cell. The CPM side is EXACT (centroid residual 0). The vertex epithelium is a regular HEXAGONAL sheet at the target area (36 hexagons, area 25.0 each) mapped 1:1 onto the blueprint cells (sub-cell residual: RMS 1.60 um, max 2.44 um). The 12 immune cells are overlay islands exactly on their centroids, and the fields are overlaid on the tissue rather than meshed: no guard-ring or medium polygons remain.

investigations.name: substrate-divergence-counterfactual
investigations.title: Mechanics-dominated counterfactual (positive control)
investigations.objective: When MECHANICS (not the shared mechanism) drives the outcome, does the equivalence test correctly REJECT -- i.e. does it have the power to detect a real substrate difference?
investigations.claim: RE-RUN 2026-11-05 (reviewer: "auto-reconnect isn't working here"). Reconnect WAS on; it is now also faster (merged 4-way vertices detach at p_4 = 1 per unit time instead of 0.1, T1 at 0.2 x side), and the playback's vertex panel counts neighbour exchanges frame by frame. In this regime the vertex run still makes only 3 exchanges in 80 steps (vs 74 in the Sego run): with 15 A cells (nearly all on the border) and a one-row B stripe, nothing shrinks a junction to the T1 threshold, so the vertex clusters keep their topology while the CPM blobs flow -- the substrate difference this control is built to expose, not a disabled reconnect. Equivalence is still REJECTED (same 0.775, cross 0.450, Delta +0.325 vs +/-0.10). Earlier reading (2026-10-28): In a MECHANICS-DOMINATED regime (strong differential adhesion + a strong chemoattractant gradient, no shared rules/ODE), the spatial equivalence test still REJECTS equivalence after the 2026-10-28 vertex revision. Cross-backend spatial agreement is 0.417 vs same-backend 0.775 (diff +0.358 > margin 0.10), now with mechanics-stochastic replicates, so the same-backend baseline is a genuine stochastic null rather than 1.0 by construction. It remains the POSITIVE CONTROL: the same test that finds the Sego model fate-equivalent detects a substrate difference here. REVISED MECHANISM: the earlier attribution (vertex A cells climbing the gradient to y~17.9 while CPM stays at ~10.7) was an artifact of the old uncalibrated vertex chemotaxis. With chemotactic drift calibrated to the CPM (saturating), neither substrate moves A far (CPM mean y 11.0 -> 11.0, vertex 10.7 -> 10.1). The divergence is now positional / sorting dynamics, not migration direction, and is not yet causally isolated.
